name: General
title: Political Compass Test with Bias Score | CoreOpinion
desc: Take the political compass test that reveals your framing bias. 100 ideological statements, every position asked twice, matched against 11 ideologies from communism to libertarianism.
keywords: political compass test, political quiz, political ideology test, framing bias, where do I stand politically, political compass 2026, libertarian authoritarian quiz, economic left right test, free political test, am I liberal or conservative, political spectrum quiz, political compass with bias score

com.name: Communism
com.desc: Revolutionary socialism aiming for a classless society where all major property is held in common.

ss.name: State Socialism
ss.desc: A planned economy run by a strong state that owns industry and directs production.

ds.name: Democratic Socialism
ds.desc: Socialism pursued through elections: public ownership expanded within a democratic state.

sd.name: Social Democracy
sd.desc: A regulated market economy with strong unions, high taxes, and a universal welfare state.

ls.name: Libertarian Socialism
ls.desc: Anti-authoritarian socialism: worker self-management and voluntary federation instead of state power.

cen.name: Centrism
cen.desc: Pragmatic politics of the middle: compromise, institutions, and gradual reform over ideology.

lib.name: Libertarianism
lib.desc: Minimal state, maximal individual liberty: free markets and personal freedom in all things.

con.name: Conservatism
con.desc: Preserving what works: tradition, rule of law, family, and a market economy under stable institutions.

nc.name: National Conservatism
nc.desc: Nation-first conservatism: strong borders, national culture, and sovereignty over global integration.

ns.name: National Socialism
ns.desc: The totalitarian ideology of Nazi Germany: ethnic nationalism, a leader state, and racial hierarchy.

mon.name: Monarchism
mon.desc: Rule anchored in a hereditary crown: continuity, hierarchy, and authority above party politics.

bank.q: Private ownership of factories, land, and major industry should be abolished and placed in the hands of the people.
Seizing private property in the name of the people has produced nothing in history but poverty, fear, and mass graves.
Capitalism is the only economic system that has ever lifted masses of people out of poverty.
Capitalism survives by exploiting workers: the profit at the top is unpaid labour taken from the bottom.
A civilised society guarantees every citizen housing, healthcare, and food, no matter what.
Generous welfare breeds dependency and rewards people who choose not to work.
Billionaires should not exist; wealth beyond a certain point should simply be taxed away.
Punishing success with confiscatory taxes kills the ambition that drives all human progress.
My race is superior to others in many ways.
No race is superior to another; every human being has equal inherent worth.
Some ethnic groups simply commit far more violent crime than others, and pretending otherwise is a lie.
Differences in crime rates come from poverty and circumstances, not from the ethnic groups themselves.
Mass immigration is slowly erasing the native culture and character of Western nations.
Immigration enriches a nation with new talent, energy, and ideas.
Every illegal immigrant should be deported. No exceptions, no apologies.
People who have built honest lives here for years deserve a path to legal status, not a knock on the door at dawn.
Belonging to a nation is a matter of blood and heritage, not a piece of paper.
Anyone who embraces a country, its laws, and its culture can become a full member of that nation.
What this country needs is a strong leader willing to act without being blocked by parliaments and courts.
Concentrating power in a single leader has always ended in corruption, fear, and repression.
Democracy, for all its flaws, is the only legitimate source of political power.
The masses are too uninformed and too easily manipulated for important decisions to be left to a popular vote.
A hereditary monarch standing above party politics gives a nation stability that elected politicians never can.
No one deserves power or privilege because of the family they were born into.
Real change has always required force; no ruling class has ever surrendered its power voluntarily.
Political violence is never justified in a society where change can happen through the ballot.
People must be free to say things that are deeply offensive, even hateful, without fear of the law.
Speech that dehumanises minorities is not free expression, it is a weapon, and the law should treat it as one.
If mass surveillance stops terror attacks and protects children, only the guilty have a reason to object.
A state that watches everyone treats every citizen as a suspect.
Some crimes are so evil that the only just answer is execution.
The state should never hold the power to kill its own citizens.
Violent criminals belong behind bars for a long time; rehabilitation is a luxury for people who never met a victim.
Ever harsher sentences have never made a society safer; treatment and prevention do.
An armed citizenry is the final check against a tyrannical government.
Easy access to guns turns arguments into funerals and schools into targets.
A nation that abandons God abandons the moral foundation it was built on.
Laws must rest on reason and evidence, never on any religion.
Abortion is a private medical decision between a woman and her doctor. Full stop.
Abortion ends a human life, and a society that shrugs at that has lost its moral compass.
Trans women are women and trans men are men, and the law should recognise them as such.
Biological sex is a fact of nature; no declaration and no surgery can change it.
The traditional family of father, mother, and children is the bedrock of civilisation and must be defended.
Love makes a family; two fathers or two mothers raise children just as well.
Men and women are naturally suited to different roles, and society works best when it respects that.
Gender roles are cages built by history, not by biology.
Climate change is an existential emergency; our economies must be transformed even at painful cost.
Climate policy has become a religion of the elites, and working people are the sacrifice.
Endless economic growth on a finite planet is a suicide pact.
Growth and innovation, not restraint and rationing, are what actually solve environmental problems.
Healthcare is a human right and must be free at the point of use for everyone.
Government-run healthcare means queues, rationing, and a bureaucrat deciding whether you are worth treating.
Workers create all wealth and deserve far more power over the companies they work for.
Unions protect the lazy, strangle businesses, and have driven entire industries into the ground.
Inherited fortunes entrench a class of people who never earned anything in their lives.
Parents have every right to pass on what they built; the state has no claim on a dead person’s life work.
When everyone gets the same chances, unequal outcomes are just: some people simply work harder.
Equal opportunity is a myth told by the winners; the lottery of birth decides most of who succeeds.
Free trade across open borders has made humanity richer than any other policy in history.
Globalisation gutted our industries and sold out working families to the lowest bidder abroad.
Nations must give up some sovereignty to bodies like the UN and EU if humanity is to solve global problems.
No unelected international body should ever be able to override the laws of a sovereign nation.
Peace is kept by strength; a nation unwilling to fight will end up ruled by one that is.
Military spending is theft from the hungry; wars enrich arms makers and bury the poor.
Children should be taught to be proud of their nation’s history, not ashamed of it.
A nation that whitewashes its crimes in the classroom is lying to its own children.
A country of many cultures living side by side is stronger than any monoculture.
Multiculturalism has produced parallel societies that share a passport and nothing else.
Some religions are simply incompatible with Western values.
Every faith deserves the same freedom and the same respect under the law.
Adults own their own bodies; the state has no right to punish anyone for what they choose to consume.
Drug legalisation surrenders the streets to addiction and hands the profits to the cartels.
Sex work is work, and criminalising it only endangers the people who do it.
Prostitution is paid exploitation, and a decent society does not put a licence on it.
Parents, not the state, should decide which values their children are taught.
Public schools must teach shared civic values, even when parents object.
Complex policy should be decided by scientists and experts, not by politicians chasing votes.
Rule by unelected experts is just tyranny with a diploma.
The mainstream media exists to protect the powerful and manufacture consent.
Independent journalism, whatever its flaws, is a pillar no democracy can stand without.
Governments must force platforms to delete dangerous misinformation.
Letting the state decide what is true is the end of free thought.
Breaking an unjust law is not a crime. It is a duty.
If everyone obeyed only the laws they personally agree with, civilisation would collapse.
The interests of workers and the interests of owners are fundamentally opposed.
Employers and employees prosper together; class war is a fantasy that impoverishes both.
As machines replace human work, every citizen must be guaranteed an unconditional basic income.
Paying people to do nothing is the fastest way to destroy the meaning of work.
Housing is a right; no one should own ten apartments while families sleep in cars.
Rent caps and housing mandates have wrecked every housing market they have ever touched.
The police need more power and fewer restraints to take back the streets.
Hand the police unchecked power and the innocent are always the first casualties.
Every young citizen owes their country a period of military or civil service.
The state does not own young people’s lives; conscription is forced labour.
Major national decisions should be put directly to the people in referendums.
Referendums reduce complex questions to slogans and mob emotion.
Traditions carry the accumulated wisdom of generations and should not be discarded lightly.
Worship of tradition means letting the dead govern the living.
People are fundamentally selfish, and any system that pretends otherwise will fail.
People are fundamentally cooperative; it is unjust systems that make them cruel.

heroSub: 100 ideological statements answered on a six-point scale. Every position is asked twice with opposite framing, so your results show where you land, which ideologies you match, and how much wording bends your answers.
